title: Low-input Fire Bear Smith of Kitava Build Guide
shortTitle: Low-input Fire Bear Smith of Kitava
summary: A staged Smith of Kitava bear build: Molten Crash fissures drive the fire triggers while you manually maintain buffs and charges. 0.5 changed which actions feed Fire Spell on Hit and Cast on Elemental Ailment.
description: Complete Path of Exile 2 Low-input Fire Bear Smith of Kitava build guide on the 0.5.4 baseline.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: A molten bear-form Smith of Kitava crossing fiery fissures and falling embers

sections.title: Build Overview
paragraphs: This build is the Low-input Fire Bear, not a 'zero-button' build. The finished map loop is low-effort because trigger gems fire automatically, but the character still requires you to maintain active buffs, build Glory and Rage, and keep the Rage/Endurance recovery loop alive. In 0.5, Ancestral Cry steps and Walking Calamity no longer feed Fire Spell on Hit or Cast on Elemental Ailment directly; walking over Molten Crash fissures is the current trigger path described by the maintained guide.

That change matters because old footage can look visually identical while using a dead trigger source. Reproduce fissure creation, walk-over detonation, Living Bomb and the fire-infused Comet chain one step at a time before trusting the low-input automation.
This is the highest-risk build to present as automatic: the loop still needs manually maintained buffs, and 0.5 altered which actions trigger the fire effects.
bullets: Runs automatically: Fire Spell on Hit and Cast on Elemental Ailment fire on their conditions; the fissure walk-over path drives the fire chain (per maintained guide, pending PC verification).
Maintained manually: the two active buffs the guide requires (exact identity pending PC), plus Glory/Rage generation and the Endurance Charge recovery loop.
Do not call the leveling or setup phase 'zero-button' — the preparation is real.

sections.title: Pros and Cons
pros: Strong defensive identity: high life/armour bear form suits a low-input mapping style.
The primary fissure trigger loop has current 0.5 guide coverage.
The guide separates mapping assumptions from boss assumptions.
cons: Not truly zero-button: you must keep buffs and charges maintained.
Several mechanics still need current-client reproduction.
Endgame creator setups can hide expensive dependencies.
Exact support and passive choices may change by variant.

sections.title: How the Loop Reads
paragraphs: There are two rhythms. Mapping is the low-input state: you create Molten Crash fissures and move through them; trigger gems auto-fire the fire package while you keep buffs and charges up. Bossing is a deliberate opening before the auto-loop can sustain you.
Treat the loop as: auto-triggers do the damage, but you own the buff uptime and charge recovery. If the screen goes quiet, the trigger chain broke — fix the setup, not the weapon.
bullets: Automatic: Fire Spell on Hit / Cast on Elemental Ailment on their conditions.
Manual: maintain the required buffs; sustain Glory/Rage and Endurance Charges.
0.5 trigger path: walk over Molten Crash fissures (Ancestral Cry / Walking Calamity no longer feed the fire triggers).

steps.label: Loop goes quiet in maps
steps.symptom: The trigger fire package stops firing while walking.
checks: Is a Molten Crash fissure actually under you?
Are Fire Spell on Hit / Cast on Elemental Ailment still socketed and conditioned?
Did the maintained buffs and charges drop?
steps.upgrade: Re-create a fissure and walk it; re-apply the buffs and rebuild charges. Fix the setup, not the weapon.

steps.label: Dying after entering maps
steps.symptom: Frequent deaths in T15+ or boss arenas.
checks: Which resistances are uncapped?
Is life/armour below the content tier?
Are defensive layers (Endurance Charges) active?
steps.upgrade: Cap resistances and stabilize life/armour before chasing trigger DPS.

steps.label: Single-target loop stalls
steps.symptom: Boss damage collapses after the opening.
checks: Are buffs and charges maintained through the fight?
Is the fissure walk-over trigger reproducing?
Are kill-based assumptions removed?
steps.upgrade: Rebuild the maintained buffs/charges and re-test one fissure; do not buy DPS to fix a recovery break.

steps.label: Considering trigger uniques
steps.symptom: Want the low-input automation and eyeing unique dependencies.
checks: Is the non-trigger baseline (defense, fissure trigger) already solved?
Will uniques break resist caps or drop life/armour?
Has the unique been reproduced in 0.5?
steps.upgrade: Add unique dependencies only after the loop is verified; retest, do not trade survival for automation.

steps.label: Uncertain which actions still trigger
steps.symptom: Old guide/video shows Ancestral Cry or Walking Calamity feeding the fire.
checks: Is this pre-0.5 footage?
Did you reproduce the 0.5 fissure path in client?
steps.upgrade: Trust the 0.5 fissure walk-over path; treat pre-0.5 trigger logic as dead until reproduced.

sections.title: Mapping
paragraphs: Maintain the required buffs, create fissures with Molten Crash, then move through them so the trigger chain fires. If the screen is quiet, inspect fissures first; walking without a fissure is no longer sufficient.
The automation is low-input, not absent: you still keep the two required buffs and the charge recovery loop active. Treat buff uptime as part of the clear, not as optional.
bullets: Automatic: Fire Spell on Hit / Cast on Elemental Ailment on the fissure path.
Manual: keep the two required buffs and Endurance Charge recovery alive.
Track Rage, Glory and Endurance Charges before calling the loop permanent.

sections.title: Bossing
paragraphs: Boss opening: before the auto-loop can carry you, pre-create fissures with Molten Crash and, where used, Forge Hammer on the second weapon set. Apply the armour-break or damage-buff layer, get your buffs and Endurance Charges active, then walk the fissures so the fire triggers fire. A boss arena is a bad place to discover you are merely walking over empty ground.

Recovery after the loop breaks: if the fire package stops, do not keep walking blindly. Re-apply the maintained buffs, rebuild Glory/Rage and Endurance Charges, re-create a fissure and walk it once to confirm the chain returns before committing to the boss again. A missing trigger is a setup break, not a gear break.
bullets: Boss opening: buffs up -> fissures placed -> charges active -> walk the fissure.
Manual upkeep: keep the two required buffs and the charge loop alive throughout.
Recovery: re-buff, rebuild charges, re-test one fissure before re-engaging.

items.question: Why do I walk through enemies without triggering the fire package?
answer: In 0.5, walking or Ancestral Cry steps alone are not the trigger. Confirm that Molten Crash created fissures and that you are walking over those fissures with the correct skills socketed.
bullets: Add each trigger gem back one at a time.

items.question: Is this truly zero-button?
answer: No. It is low-input: Fire Spell on Hit and Cast on Elemental Ailment fire automatically, but you must keep the required buffs and the charge recovery loop alive. Calling the leveling build zero-button hides the preparation and leads to expensive purchases before the loop exists.
bullets: Automatic layer: trigger gems on their conditions.
Manual layer: buff upkeep and charge recovery.

items.question: What if I want a simpler Bear route?
answer: Rampage Shaman has active Rage and animation management but a more direct attack loop without the same fire-trigger dependency.
